# Synthetic exposure fixtures

The `exposure-*.jpg` files and `exposure-color-reference.json` were generated locally by `test/generate-exposure-fixtures.py`. Pixels are uniform patches and four original geometric color quadrants; no third-party photograph or downloaded ICC profile was used. The gray test JPEG is generated by Electron at runtime. The project's original code and documentation are now covered by the root MIT license; third-party and asset rights remain separated in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Tooling used only for fixture creation: Pillow 12.3.0 (its distribution LICENSE identifies MIT-CMU) and LittleCMS 2.19 bundled with Pillow. Neither is installed by npm, required by CI, shipped in the app, or added to package.json/lockfile. LittleCMS generates the sRGB ICC profile; the synthetic P3 matrix variant edits its matrix tags. Both profiles retain the generated `cprt` tag text: **No copyright, use freely**. The fixtures do not redistribute those software libraries. Tools remain in the ignored local `.test-tools` directory.

Checked-in byte fixtures and independent encoded-sRGB reference values allow Windows runner execution without Python/Pillow or network fixture generation. The existing installed Electron 44.7.0 performs all runtime decoding/conversion/canvas/worker/SQLite checks. The first test uses only small JPEGs (up to 80×40); the 36 MP performance workload is separate/manual. Accessibility input is sent through Chromium to construction-time-hidden windows; physical keyboard, native-dialog and visual QA remain distinct.
